Surah 15 (al-Hijr), verses 1–5

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1} Allah, exalting His Book and praising it, says: {These are the verses of the Book}; that is, the verses that indicate the best of meanings and the most excellent aims, {and a clear Qur'an}: making the realities clear with the finest and most explicit wording, and the most indicative of the intended meaning.

{2} This necessitates that creation submit to it, surrender to its judgment, and receive it with acceptance, joy and delight. As for those who meet this great blessing by rejecting it and disbelieving in it, they are among the deniers and the misguided, and there will come upon them a time when they will wish that they were Muslims; that is, submitting to its rulings. That will be when the veil is lifted and the first signs of the Hereafter and the premonitions of death appear, for they will wish, in all the states of the Hereafter, that they had been Muslims, but the time of possibility will have passed. Yet in this world they are deluded.

{3} So {leave them to eat and enjoy themselves}, with their pleasures, {and let hope distract them}; that is, they hope to remain in this world, and this diverts them from the Hereafter. {But they will come to know}: that what they are upon is false, and that their deeds have gone to waste, to their loss, and let them not be deceived by Allah's respite, for this is His way with the nations.

{4} {And We never destroyed a town} that deserved punishment {except that it had a known decree}: a determined term for its destruction.

{5} {No nation can precede its term, nor can they delay it}: that is, sins inevitably have their effect, even if it is delayed.

{6} That is: the deniers said to Muhammad (ﷺ), mockingly and sarcastically: ﴿O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down﴾, according to your claim, ﴿indeed you are a madman﴾, for you think that we will follow you and abandon what we found our fathers upon, merely on the basis of your word.

{7–8} ﴿Why do you not bring us the angels﴾ to testify for you to the truth of what you have brought, ﴿if you are among the truthful?﴾ Since you have not brought the angels, you are not truthful. This is among the greatest of wrongdoing and ignorance. As for wrongdoing, it is evident: this is audacity toward God and obstinacy in specifying signs which He did not choose, while the purpose and the proof were accomplished without them, through the many signs that indicate the truth of what he brought. As for ignorance, they failed to recognise their own benefit from their harm, for there is no good for them in the sending down of the angels. Rather, God does not send down the angels except with the truth, and there is no respite for whoever does not follow it and submit to it. ﴿And they would not have been reprieved﴾; that is, when the angels descend, if they do not believe, and they will not believe. Their demand for the sending down of the angels was thus a hastening of their own destruction and ruin, for faith is not in their hands; it is in the hand of God. ﴿Even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We gathered against them everything in front of them, they would not have believed unless God willed, but most of them are ignorant.﴾

{9} The Great Qur'an suffices them as a sign, if they were truthful. For this reason He says here: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder﴾; that is, the Qur'an, in which is a reminder of everything, of questions and clear proofs, and in which whoever desires to be mindful is reminded. ﴿And indeed, We are its guardian﴾; that is, during its revelation and after its revelation. Thus no distorter distorts any of its meanings without God raising up for him someone who makes the clear truth manifest. This is among the greatest of God's signs and blessings upon His believing servants. And among its preservation is that God protects its people from their enemies, and does not give any enemy power over them to uproot them.

{16} The Most High says, explaining His complete power and His mercy toward His creation: ﴿And We have placed in the sky constellations﴾; that is, stars like great lofty signs by which one is guided in the darknesses of land and sea. ﴿And We have adorned it for the observers﴾: for were it not for the stars, the sky would not have this radiant appearance and wondrous form. This invites the observers to reflect upon it, to contemplate its meanings, and to infer from it the existence of its Originator.

{17} ﴿And We have guarded it from every accursed devil﴾: whenever one steals the hearing, piercing meteors pursue him. Thus the sky remains outwardly beautified with bright stars, and inwardly guarded and protected from calamities.

{18} ﴿Except one who steals a hearing﴾; that is, [except] that at some times some devils may steal the hearing secretly and furtively. ﴿So there follows him a clear flaming meteor﴾; that is, a clear, shining one that kills him or deranges him. Sometimes the meteor overtakes him before the devil can convey it to his companion, so the news of the sky is cut off from the earth. And sometimes he conveys it to his companion before the meteor reaches him, so he adds to it and tells a hundred lies along with it, and proofs himself by that word which was heard from the sky.

{19} ﴿And the earth – We have spread it out﴾; that is, We made it vast, a extent that enables human beings and all animals to move about its expanses, to take from its provisions, and to dwell in its regions. ﴿And We have cast therein firmly set mountains﴾; that is, great mountains that, by Allah's permission, keep the earth from shaking and make it firm so that it does not move. ﴿And We have caused to grow therein of every well-balanced thing﴾; that is, of every beneficial, valued thing upon which the servants and the lands depend: including palm trees, grapevines, various kinds of trees, varieties of plants, and minerals.

{20} ﴿And We have made for you therein means of livelihood﴾: from tilling, from livestock, and from various kinds of earnings and crafts, ﴿and [for] those for whom you are not providers﴾; that is, We have bestowed upon you servants, maidservants, and livestock for your benefit and welfare, and their provision is not upon you; rather, Allah has entrusted them to you and undertaken to provide for them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 15, verses 51–56:

{51} God Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): {And inform them about the guests of Abraham}; that is, about that wondrous story. For in your relating to them the accounts of the messengers and what befell them is what necessitates for them lessons and emulation of them, especially Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil), whose religion God has commanded us to follow. His guests were the noble angels, whom God honored by making them his guests.

{52} {When they entered upon him and said, "Peace."}; that is, they greeted him with peace, and he returned their greeting. {He said, "Indeed, we are fearful of you."}; that is, frightened. For when they entered upon him, and he considered them guests, he went quickly to his household and brought them their hospitality: a roasted calf. He presented it to them, but when he saw that their hands did not reach toward it, he feared they were thieves or the like. Then they said to him:

{53} {"Fear not. Indeed, we give you good tidings of a learned boy."}: and he is Isaac (peace be upon him). This good news included that he would be a male, not a female. {Learned}; that is, abundant in knowledge. And in another verse: {And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous}.

{54} {He said} to them, astonished at this good news: {"Do you give me good tidings [of a child] when old age has touched me?"}: and a kind of despair of it had set in. {So by what [means] do you give me good tidings?}; that is, in what manner do you give me good tidings when the means have been lost?!

{55} {They said, "We have given you good tidings in truth"}: which has no doubt in it; for God is capable of all things, and you especially, O people of this household, {the mercy of God and His blessings be upon you}; so the grace and kindness of God toward you is not to be deemed strange. {So do not be of the despairing}: those who consider the occurrence of good to be unlikely. Rather, continue to hope for the grace, kindness, goodness and bounty of God.

{56} Abraham answered them with his saying: {And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except the misguided?}: those who have no knowledge of their Lord and the perfection of His power. As for one whom God has blessed with guidance and great knowledge, there is no path to despair for him, because he knows from the abundance of the causes, means and ways to the mercy of God a great deal.
Then, when they gave him this good news, he knew that they were messengers sent for an important matter.

{57} That is, Abraham (peace be upon him) said to the angels: ﴿What is your business, O messengers?﴾ That is: what is your affair, and for what purpose were you sent?

{58} ﴿They said: "We have been sent to a guilty people."﴾ That is: their corruption has increased and their evil has grown great, so that We may punish them and requite them.

{59–60} ﴿Except the family of Lot,﴾ that is, except Lot and his household, ﴿except his wife; We have decreed that she will be among those who remain behind.﴾ That is, among those who remain to be destroyed by the punishment. As for Lot, We will bring him out with his household and save them from it. Abraham then began to argue with the messengers about their destruction and to reason with them, so it was said to him: ﴿O Abraham, turn away from this. The command of your Lord has come, and a punishment that cannot be averted will surely reach them.﴾ So they left him.

{61–62} ﴿When the messengers came to the family of Lot,﴾ Lot said to them: ﴿You are a people unknown to me.﴾ That is, I do not know you, and I do not know who you are.

{63} ﴿They said: "Rather, we have brought you that about which they used to doubt."﴾ That is, we have brought you their punishment, about which they used to be in doubt and to deny you when you threatened them with it.

{64} ﴿And we have brought you the truth,﴾ which is not a jest. ﴿And indeed we are truthful,﴾ in what we have told you.

{65} ﴿So travel with your family in the dark part of the night,﴾ that is, during its course, when eyes are asleep and no one knows of your departure. ﴿And let none of you look back,﴾ that is, rather hasten and move quickly, ﴿and proceed where you are commanded.﴾ It is as if they had a guide with them who showed them where to head.

{66} ﴿And We conveyed that matter to him,﴾ that is, We informed him with a report that admits no doubt: ﴿that the last remnant of these people would be cut off at dawn.﴾ That is, the punishment that would overwhelm and uproot them would strike them at morning.

{67–69} ﴿And the people of the city came, rejoicing.﴾ That is, the city in which Lot lived. They rejoiced, each telling the other about Lot's guests, their beauty and their strength over them, because they intended to commit the abomination with them. They came until they reached Lot's house and began pressing Lot concerning his guests, while Lot sought refuge from them and said: ﴿Indeed, these are my guests, so do not disgrace me. And fear Allah and do not humiliate me.﴾ That is, first be mindful of Allah, even though there is no fear of Allah among you; do not disgrace me regarding my guests, and do not violate them in a monstrous act.

{70} ﴿They said,﴾ in reply to his words ﴿"do not humiliate me"﴾ only: ﴿Have we not forbidden you from [hosting] the people of the worlds?﴾ That is, from hosting them. We had already warned you, and whoever is warned has been given an excuse.

{71–72} ﴿Lot said to them,﴾ because of the severity of the situation that had befallen him: ﴿These are my daughters, if you must act.﴾ They paid no heed to his words. For this reason Allah said to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿By your life, they were wandering blindly in their intoxication.﴾ This intoxication is the intoxication of love for the abomination, which made them unconcerned with reproach or blame.

{73} When the messengers made their condition clear to him, the distress and anguish that Lot had been suffering left him. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 15, verses 80–84:

{80} Allah the Exalted informs about the People of al-Hijr (al-Hijr), who were the people of Salih, who dwelt in the rock-dwellings known in the land of the Hijaz: that they denied the Messengers. That is, they denied Salih, and whoever denies a Messenger has denied all the Messengers, because their call is one and the same. Their denial of one of them was not a denial of his person alone, but of the truth he brought, which all the Messengers shared in bringing.

{81} {And We gave them Our signs}: which indicate the truth of what Salih brought them, among which was that she-camel, which was one of Allah's great signs. {But they turned away from them}: out of arrogance and tyranny against Allah.

{82} {And they used to hew out homes from the mountains, secure}: from fears, at peace in their dwellings. Had they been thankful for the blessing and believed their Prophet Salih (peace be upon him), Allah would have poured down provision upon them and honoured them with various kinds of reward, both hastened and deferred. But when they denied, hamstrung the she-camel, rebelled against the command of their Lord, and said: {O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful}.

{83} {So the Shout seized them at morning}: their hearts were torn within their bodies, and they were left in their homes, prostrate and dead, along with the disgrace and the continuing curse that follows.

{84} {So what they used to earn did not avail them}: because when the command of Allah comes, it is not repelled by a multitude of soldiers, nor by a strength of helpers, nor by an abundance of wealth.

And the Most High has done so: no one openly mocked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and what he brought except that Allah destroyed him and killed him in the worst manner of killing.

{96} Then He mentioned their attribute, and that just as they harm you, O Messenger of Allah, they also harm Allah: {those who set up with Allah another god}, who is their Lord, their Creator and their Disposer. {But they are going to know} - the outcome of their deeds when they arrive at the Resurrection.

{97} {And We certainly know that your breast becomes constricted by what they say} - of denial and mockery against you. We are capable of uprooting them with punishment and hastening upon them what they deserve; but Allah gives them respite, and does not neglect them.

So the Prophet (ﷺ) complied with the command of his Lord, and he did not cease being constant in worship until the certainty came to him from his Lord, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him abundantly.
